newsitem.title: UK: Ex-GATT, WTO head becomes new BP chairman.
newsitem.headline: Ex-GATT, WTO head becomes new BP chairman.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc on Thursday said its deputy chairman Peter Sutherland has agreed to replace David Simon as non-executive chairman.
Simon gave up his post last month when he was appointed as minister of European Trade and Competitiveness of Britain's new Labour government.
Sutherland, 51, was director-general of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) in 1993 and subsequently served as director-general of the World Trade Organisation until May 1995.
The Dublin-educated barrister has been BP's deputy chairman since July 1995 and had been on the oil giant's board from 1990 to 1993.
In 1981, Sutherland was appointed Ireland's Attorney General and four years later he became a Commissioner at the European Commission with responsibility for competition policy.
"I am delighted and honoured to take up this position in one of the United Kingdom and Europe's leading companies," Sutherland said in a statement.
Sutherland said he will remain chairman of the European arm of investment bank Goldman Sachs.
